title: Live log tail tap with trace-enhanced adaptive sampling and tenant budgeted streaming
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Scope: Build a production-grade 'live tail tap' capability in the ingest plane that lets engineers and on-call responders tail a live subset of structured logs with minimal cost and safe privacy defaults. The feature will attach a lightweight sidecar transformer to the ingest gateway that can: 1) derive a short session fingerprint and normalize trace linkage fields, 2) apply trace-enhanced adaptive sampling rules (favoring traces with errors/high latency or anomalous metric spikes), and 3) stream selected events to a tenant-scoped live-tail endpoint backed by a budgeted streaming credit pool. Out of scope: Full rework of existing batch reingest; long-term cold storage changes.

Design summary: Sidecar transformer sits after parsing in the ingest pipeline. It computes a session fingerprint (HMAC over stable fields) and a normalized trace_key (prefer trace_id > span_guid > session_fingerprint). Sampling policy is multi-armed: deterministic keep for error-tagged events, priority boost for traces with recent SLO breaches observed in metrics, and probabilistic reservoir sampling for background traffic. Tenants receive a configurable credits quota; live-tail consumes credits by event size and retention time. When credits exhausted, serve degraded mode (100ms-headline sample or discontinue non-error streams). All transformations are logged to an audit topic.

Privacy & redaction: Default policy strips PII fields (email, ssn-like patterns) at the transformer layer. Tenants can opt-in to keep additional fields via security-reviewed flag. Any retention of raw payloads must go through KMS-protected blob storage and will be tracked.

APIs & UX hooks: Add a new console live-tail route with query filters (trace_key, service, severity, time window) and a throttle control exposing remaining credits. Provide a simple GET /live-tail/{tenant}?q=... that opens an SSE stream. Instrument tracing hooks that correlate live-tail actions with request spans for audit and debugging.

Backpressure & reliability: Transformer uses bounded worker pools and request-level backpressure to avoid head-of-line blocking. We will reuse the existing ingest backpressure token-bucket and emit metrics for queue depth, drop rate, and credit exhaustion events.

Metrics & alerts: New metrics: live_tail_streams_active, live_tail_events_streamed, live_tail_credit_used, live_tail_credit_exhausted, live_tail_sampling_rate_by_priority, live_tail_error_forward_rate. Alert on credit exhaustion events for high-tier tenants and on streaming latency > 500ms tail-to-client.

Rollout plan: 1) internal staging prototype with synthetic high-cardinality traffic (2 weeks), 2) opt-in beta for internal teams and two low-risk customers (4 weeks), 3) gradual ramp with observability dashboards and cost thresholds (2 weeks), 4) GA release after 2 successful weeks in ramp.

Success criteria: Prototype can sustain 10k events/s with median tail-to-client latency < 200ms under normal load; sampling keeps error trace coverage > 95% while reducing stream volume by >= 70% vs naive tailing; no PII leaks in default mode; tenants can cap monthly live-tail spend via credits.
success_criteria: 1) median tail latency < 200ms at 10k events/s in staging; 2) error trace coverage >= 95% under adaptive sampling; 3) live-tail reduces total streamed volume >= 70% vs naive tail; 4) no default PII leaks in 10k random sample audit; 5) billing/credits tracked per tenant in console.
design_decisions:
- Use a stateless transformer that emits enrichments to the ingest stream instead of mutating primary payloads.
- Session fingerprint chosen instead of session cookie parsing to support heterogeneous clients.
- Deterministic sampling keys based on normalized trace_key to ensure downstream replays match selection.
- Tenant budget model prevents noisy tenants from accidental cost spikes; credits consumed deterministically by bytes + retention window.
test_plan: Unit tests for transformer logic (session fingerprinting, redaction, sampling), integration tests with Loki-forwarder in staging, chaos testing for worker pool saturation, synthetic traffic runs to validate sampling coverage and credit accounting, security fuzz for PII detection. End-to-end verification: open live-tail, cause a traced error, assert that error trace appears in tail within SLAs.
rollout_plan: Stage -> internal beta -> tenant opt-in cohort -> 50% ramp -> GA. Monitor key metrics and keep fast rollback flag that disables live-tail streaming per region. First-phase opt-in customers: infra-oncall, infra-experiments team.
migration_notes: Minimal: live-tail attaches as an optional path to existing ingest pipeline. No mandatory schema changes. Will add audit-forwarding topic for transformer changes; maintain compatibility with Loki/ELK adapters by preserving canonical trace_key header.

notes: Feature ties into incident responder flow; prefer conservative defaults. Keep audit trail on any tenant opt-ins for extended retention. Coordinate with Billing for credits accounting and with Security for any tenant-level exceptions.
